quizzes.title: India and BRICS: MCQ Practice
quizzes.passage:
The World Happiness Report is an annual ranking of countries based on how people evaluate their own lives. Respondents are asked to rate their lives on a numbered scale, and the results are read together with six key indicators. These indicators are GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom, generosity and perception of corruption. Because the report looks at these factors together, it helps countries assess development beyond GDP alone.

The report does not compare countries only on one global list. It also places countries within regional and economic groups, so that a country can be seen against its neighbours and against the other members of BRICS. India is one of the countries studied in South Asia, and its position can be read alongside the positions of its neighbours. Such comparisons show how a country stands relative to others in its own group.

India's place in the 2026 edition can also be compared with its earlier position, because rankings can move from one edition to the next. A change in rank is shown alongside the country's score, so the movement and the level of well-being can be read together. Areas where a country has improved are also identified in the report.

The 2026 report was released on International Day of Happiness, which is observed every year on 20 March. The report emphasises well-being as a policy goal.

questions.q: Which BRICS nation ranked highest in the 2026 World Happiness Report?
questions.explanation: China was the highest-ranked BRICS nation, placed 65th overall.

questions.q: India's 2026 rank was an improvement from which earlier position?
questions.explanation: India improved from 118th in the previous ranking to its 2026 position.

questions.q: Which two areas were identified as areas of improvement for India in the 2026 report?
options: Social support and healthy life expectancy
questions.explanation: The report names social support and healthy life expectancy as India's areas of improvement.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): India ranked below Nepal and Pakistan in the 2026 report.
Reason (R): Sri Lanka was placed 134th in the 2026 report.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but Sri Lanka's rank does not explain India's position relative to Nepal and Pakistan.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Russia   ->   A. 104th
II. Iran   ->   B. 99th
III. Nepal   ->   C. 79th
IV. Pakistan   ->   D. 97th
questions.explanation: Russia was 79th, Iran 97th, Nepal 99th and Pakistan 104th in the 2026 report.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India and BRICS in the 2026 report:
I. India ranked above Bangladesh.
II. Russia ranked above China.
III. Pakistan ranked above Iran.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only the first statement is correct, since China (65th) ranked above Russia (79th) and Iran (97th) ranked above Pakistan (104th).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India in the 2026 report:
I. India ranked above Nepal.
II. India ranked below Pakistan.
III. India ranked above Sri Lanka.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements II and III are correct, while India ranked below Nepal (99th), so statement I is wrong.

quizzes.title: Social Media and Youth: MCQ Practice
quizzes.passage:
The 2026 World Happiness Report examines how social media use relates to happiness among young people. The report looks at life satisfaction across age groups, comparing how people in different age brackets rate their lives. It also considers how much time young people spend on these platforms, rather than treating all use as the same. The study is therefore about patterns of use as well as the simple fact of using these platforms.

Life satisfaction in the report is measured through people's own ratings of their lives, which allows the results to be compared across groups and countries. The age comparisons are drawn from the same survey data that produces the country rankings. The findings are presented as a set of key insights. Some of these insights concern developing countries, where the effects of digital tools are discussed separately.

The report also describes situations in which the same tools bring strain. Its findings suggest that the amount of use matters, since some levels of use are associated with lower well-being than others. Taken together, these insights help show how young people are faring in a digital environment.

The report was released on International Day of Happiness, and it is part of the annual series published under the World Happiness Report name.

questions.q: According to the report, which group is the most vulnerable to social media use?
options: Elderly men using social media over 3 hours a day
Adolescent girls using social media over 5 hours a day
Young boys aged 10-14 using social media over 4 hours a day
Working adults using social media over 6 hours a day
questions.explanation: The report identifies adolescent girls who use social media for more than five hours a day as the most vulnerable group.

questions.q: In which group of countries was the age-based pattern of youth life satisfaction observed?
options: Finland, Iceland, Denmark and Costa Rica
United States, Canada, Australia and New Zealand
questions.explanation: The pattern of lower youth life satisfaction was observed in the United States, Canada, Australia and New Zealand.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Youth aged 15 to 24 report lower life satisfaction than people aged 60 and above.
Reason (R): The report provides insights into mental health and digital behaviour trends.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the report's coverage of mental health and digital trends does not explain the age gap.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Developing countries like India   ->   A. Lower life satisfaction than those aged 60 and above
II. Excessive use in the same settings   ->   B. Stress and anxiety
III. Heavy social media use   ->   C. Digital access improves education and connectivity
IV. Youth aged 15 to 24   ->   D. Decline in mental health and comparison-driven stress
questions.explanation: Digital access improves education in developing countries, excessive use causes stress, heavy use is linked with mental health decline, and youth report lower life satisfaction.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the report's findings on social media:
I. Youth aged 15 to 24 report lower life satisfaction than those aged 60 and above.
II. Adolescent girls using social media for less than five hours a day are the most vulnerable group.
III. In developing countries like India, excessive social media use causes stress and anxiety.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while the most vulnerable group is those using social media for more than five hours a day.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about social media use in the report:
I. The age-based pattern was observed in Australia.
II. Youth aged 15 to 24 report higher life satisfaction than those aged 60 and above.
III. Excessive digital use in developing countries is linked with improved happiness.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since youth report lower, not higher, life satisfaction and excessive use causes stress.

questions.q: What does the report link heavy social media use with?
options: Decline in mental health and comparison-driven stress
questions.explanation: The report links heavy use with a decline in mental health and comparison-driven stress.
